title: MV I'm trying to learn to make my own plugins for my own game, however, I can't seem to understand how to use javascript for making anything...

posts.author: PoopsyTheDuck
posts.body:

I tried looking up plugin templates and even reading the existing one I have, nothing.
I should mention that the reason I want to make my own plugins is because I don't want to rely on existing ones. There's nothing wrong with relying on existing ones, however, I want to know javascript properly for plugins of various kinds, such as a sketchpad (drawing app), games within games, using a cursor like a point and click game and even make pokemon like plugins for mv.
Please be patient with me, since I have a hard time understanding tutorials using text, I work best with videos but even videos which I tried to watch I didn't understand how they did it with javascript.
I also want to learn javascript because to be honest, programming for game development is really fun for me, even though it's hard sometimes.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Remember to use the help file with the F1 key in RPG Maker. There is also a link to the
MV help here
or
MZ help here
. There is also the
MV API
or
MZ API here
. There is a fantastic compiled list that
Archeia compiled list here
. It is much easier for finding specific calls in many instances. There are also many
specifc threads
.
Programming with RPG Maker MV or MZ is different. I had my MCSD in HTML5 from Microsoft. I already had a background, but this is a bit different. If you don't, there are many courses that can teach you the basics of Javascript:
Coursera
,
FreeCodeCamp
,
Udacity
,
Udemy
, or
W3schools
. Archeia and I have a
thread here to teach people how to learn Javascript
.
After you know the basics, you need to know how to attach it to RPG Maker. The Unpro has a series on
how to make plugins
. Quxios also has a
tutorial
to get started. The company did release a tutorial a while back that we can find in
WaybackMachine
.
My simple plan would be:
Read the help file
Read the API
Check Archeia's thread on learning Javascript
Check Unpro's playlist on plugin making
Pick a course from the list
Start simple with a Hello World, attribute modifier, or item creation in RPG Maker
Edited: updated for clarity

posts.author: Kadajah
posts.body:
Some masters have already answered you here. I don't have much to contribute, but I'd just say that if you have a little time, start with HTML and CSS. This will give you a familiar foundation with lines of code and some understanding of the elements you can manipulate with JavaScript. It's absolutely not mandatory, but the more you learn about languages, the easier it becomes to understand new concepts and applications.
Start slowly, start small, but don't ever appear shy. Never be shy about asking questions or showing your projects!

Well, it depends; HTML and CSS have nothing to do with plugin development in RPG Maker (unless you are doing some really crazy stuff).
The best to learn is probably a mix of reading tutorials here in the forum (they are specialized on plugin development which is important) and reading some plugins from various (not just one) plugin creators, the more varied your sources are, the better you can see the standard code conventions and determine which are good and which are not so good progamming styles.
Maybe start with something easy, like
- adding a shutdown button to the title screen
- adding a credits page to the title screen (my solution for some inspiration:
https://play.aerosys.blog/lisa/js/plugins/MK_Credits.js
)
- making a debug menu that also changes party members, items, gold...

posts.author: Aerosys
posts.body:
I don't want to sound gate-keeperish, but the truth is, programming is super-hard to learn.
I learned programming while I studied computer science, and during this time, I also worked part-time as a programmer - that means, I always had a mentor who supervised me and gave me tips. There are many things that the usual "learn Javascript" tutorials on YouTube will not show you but are essential to create plugins or programs that not only work, but also work when your game has plugins from other creators.
Writing plugins
defensively
is essential, but takes a long time to learn.
Even after years of developing plugins for RPG Maker, I learnt new things and conventions that exist only in RPG Maker world that were crafted by experience from the community.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@PoopsyTheDuck
perhaps the following will help you understand what causes at least some of your problems:
There is a difference between learning programming (the skill itself) and learning a programming language (like Javascript, C, Pascal or whatever).
A lot of the tutorials out there are trying to teach a (programming) language only, expecting you to already know how to program something. And those tutorials are difficult for people who have not yet learned how to program with another programming language.
Those tutorials are almost worthless to someone like you, you'll need to check each tutorial as to whether it expects knowledge of programming or not first.
The skill programming itself mostly consists of mathematics and logical operations. If you can handle that, learning programming and later multiple programming languages should be easy.
But if you had problems with math in school, then it will be more difficult to learn that for you.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
PoopsyTheDuck said:
So where do I learn programming itself? What to look up?
Click to expand...
It's basically the same place, just a different focus.
after all, you can't learn to read and write without knowing a language, and the same way you can't learn to program without a programming language.
As I already mentioned above, there are tutorials that are assuming you know how to program, and there are tutorials that do not assume that but teach programming at the same time they are teaching the programming language.
Those are the ones you have to look for, but both are listed as learning a programming language.
one way to see the difference is to look at the entire course. As said by others, you can't learn programming in a day or two - in a university, it's usually a full semester of three hours a week just for the basics.
Additionally, programming is a practical skill - you can't learn it by listening to tutorials, you need to use the skill for yourself by working and doing what the tutorials say.
so as a personal estimate any tutorial that is less than 20 hours long cannot really teach programming, but only a programming language.

II've been recently playing around with MV and just wrote my first very simple plugin this week. Yes I probably just re-invented the wheel, because what I wanted to do was so simple, but hey! It's my wheel!
Seriously though. Obvious question - Do you know Javascript? It's a full scripting language so you probably won't get far even with a tutorial withought a basic knowledge of JavaScript. If you do it's mostly about knowing, or finding out, which existing systems to aliase.
Having come from a 'normal' programing environment the initial premis of RPG Maker plugins threw me a bit untill I got my head around it. You are basically making a stand alone .JS file with your code in a 'walled garden' function. Jirst you find out what existing internal routean you want to 'hijack' then you store that and write your add-on code, remember to go back to run the origonal function at the end. I did a very simple ammendment to the movement routean that let me move diagonally left or right and down when in a 'falling' movement. You can reference any in-game variables or switches etc through their ID number.
Appologies if that dosn't mean much.
I probably havent explained things properly with the corect words!
But it is doable, just don't try to climb everest before you can walk up a hill!

posts.author: ValentinaSama67
posts.body:
I don't have much to add to the conversation, since the most I can do is edit existing plugins. I just wanted to encourage you to keep learning how to code and to keep trying. Learning anything from scratch is hard, even if you are used to getting things fast, you will eventually hit walls and stumps, what will set you up to becoming good at anything, is to keep trying and failling. Normalize not being good at things from day 1. It's okay to be terrible at it actually. Reflect on your mistakes and always try to think about/search what you could've done to avoid it next time.
Watch JS tutorials, look up guides, see how other plugin creators solve certain issues through their code, with time, you will get good if you keep trying.
And know you are more than welcome to ask questions here and in the discord.
